editorial.headline: Private Guidance, Counselling and the Business of Learning
editorial.standfirst: This private education activity spans tutoring, counselling and specialist learning support, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
Private tutoring is only the most familiar expression of this activity. Its scope covers private learning guidance and counselling, including academic tutoring, health, organisational, ethics and social-guidance instruction. It also accommodates courses and educational services connected with business, tax and psychology consulting, human-resource development, mental arithmetic, personality development, family coaching, preschool tutoring, education for children and older people, and programmes intended to develop creativity, teaching potential or learning methods. The defining thread is private-sector education and guidance: practical, developmental and delivered through instruction rather than simply through advice in the abstract.

That breadth matters for the people registering the activity. A provider may build a focused tutoring practice, a preschool-support offering, a family-development programme or a more specialised learning and human-capital education business, provided the work remains within this stated field. The activity is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale, so the classification does not reserve this private education terrain for one size of operator. Its scope is expansive, but it is not shapeless: the service must still be recognisably education, courses, guidance or counselling of the kinds described.

At the national level, PMA remains TERBUKA, and foreign ownership may reach 100%. In plain terms, foreign investment can hold the full permitted stake nationally for this activity. That is a meaningful starting point for a founder assessing an education-led business, but it should not be confused with a generic statement about every operational context. The classification’s own description is the anchor: it is directed at private guidance, counselling and the many learning formats expressly included within that field.

Bali presents a clear, rather than contradictory, picture. The province permanently blocks PMA registration island-wide for Low and Medium-Low risk activities. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium. At the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, which is why the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK rather than a moratorium prohibition. A foreign founder may therefore read the position straightforwardly: national PMA ownership is open up to 100%, and Bali does not impose the stated PMA moratorium block on this activity. The relevant Bali distinction is risk at scale, not a separate foreign-ownership cap or partnership condition.
